import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' column to datetime
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])

# Set the style
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a summary of total sales per product
product_sales = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(data=product_sales, x='total', y='product', palette='viridis')

# Title and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Product', fontsize=14)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' column to datetime
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])

# Set the style
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a summary of total sales per product
product_sales = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(data=product_sales, x='total', y='product', palette='viridis')

# Title and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Product', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Product', fontsize=14)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
